52.0.0.en: “Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean. Shake thyself from the dust; arise, and sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion” [1-2].

52.0.1.en: While the prophet affirms the return of the people from captivity with a dignity they had not expected, he is in fact speaking of the return of mankind to its first place, its return to the spiritual city of God and its enjoyment of His surpassing splendor, to live free from all uncleanness as God willed for it...

52.0.2.en: God loves man and longs to bring him into glory, to live a holy, honored and glorious life; therefore the call comes here to enjoy the following divine blessings:

52.0.3.en: a. The risen, glorious life: “Awake, awake,” for she had gone down as though into the tomb, to lie in the midst of darkness and be overtaken by corruption. This is the state of Israel in Babylon, where they lost all hope of returning to their land and enjoying freedom, so they counted themselves as dead. This is the state of every man whom sin has captured, so that his inner life collapses and he loses the good will and the ability to enjoy the holy life, becoming like a dead man overtaken by corruption. He needs someone to awaken him from the death of sin and give him the new, risen life.

52.0.4.en: The Apostle says: “Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light” (Eph 5:14). “And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Eph 2:6).

52.0.5.en: Now the Savior has come to every fallen and humiliated soul to speak to her, saying: “Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee” (Ezek 16:8)... What does the spreading of His skirt over her mean but receiving her as a bride for Himself, united with Him and enjoying His risen life?! He came to her as a Bridegroom so that she might find in Him the “resurrection” and awake as from eternal death. This is what the Apostle Paul meant by saying: “For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ” (Rom 5:17).

52.0.6.en: Thus the soul is united with the Bridegroom, the Giver of life, and puts off the grave clothes and puts on the wedding garment: “Put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city” [1]. He says to her: “I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers' skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. I decked thee also with ornaments... and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD” (Ezek 16:10-14). What is this garment that poured out on her the splendor of the Lord, so that she became exceedingly beautiful and fit to be a queen, but the person of Christ Himself, in whom we are hidden, as the Apostle says: “have put on Christ” (Gal 3:27).

52.0.7.en: * It is fitting for the whole Church to exult, praising the Lord Christ, after the example of the holy women when they realized the resurrection of the Lord, who awakened mankind from sleep, giving it life and filling it with the light of faith.

52.0.8.en: St. Jerome * Today is the “feast of the Resurrection,” and it is for me a new beginning.

52.0.9.en: * The divine mystery has anointed me... which brings me to this great, radiant day, giving help to my weakness; so that He who rose from the dead on a day like this may give life to my soul also, and clothe me with the new man (Eph 4:23-24), and make me of the new creation, of those who were born of God... so that I may be ready to die with Him and rise also with Him...

52.0.10.en: Yesterday (Good Friday) the Lamb was slain and the doorposts were sprinkled with His blood... and the destroying angel passed by with his destroying sword, terrified and afraid... because we are kept safe by the precious Blood.

52.0.11.en: Yesterday I was crucified with Christ, and today I am glorified in Him!

52.0.12.en: Yesterday I died with Him, and today I am given life with Him!

52.0.13.en: Yesterday I was buried with Him, and today I rise with Him...!

52.0.14.en: Whoever was able to understand this great mystery in Christ and what He has done for us, and has not given himself to Christ, has given Him nothing!

52.0.15.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus b. She becomes a holy city into which no uncircumcised or unclean shall come any more, that is, strangers shall no longer trample her. As the city of God she is sanctified from all uncleanness to bear the nature of the heavenly life that befits the heavenly King.

52.0.16.en: * Now, my beloved... Satan has been slain, that tyrant who is against the whole world, so we are not approaching a temporal feast but a perpetual, heavenly one...

52.0.17.en: Now death is abolished and the kingdom of Satan is destroyed; therefore everything is filled with joy and happiness...

52.0.18.en: We must approach the feast in this way, not in a defiled garment, but with our souls wrapped in clean garments. We must put on our Lord Jesus (Rom 13:4), so that we may celebrate the feast with Him.

52.0.19.en: Now we put Him on when we love virtue and hate evil; when we train ourselves in chastity and put our lusts to death; when we love righteousness and not iniquity; when we honor contentment and have a settled mind; when we do not forget the poor but open our doors to all men; when we help the weak and cast off pride.

52.0.20.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic c. She shakes herself from the dust, for the soul no longer clings to temporal things but seeks first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things are added to her. She lives set free toward eternity, released from the bonds of the world.

52.1.0.en: d. She arises as a queen to sit on the throne of the kingdom [2], after having been a maidservant and a captive slave sitting in the dust, serving her masters in humiliation and shame; she rises to the right hand of the heavenly King. As the Psalmist says: “Upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir” (Ps 45:9).

52.1.1.en: e. Enjoying freedom: “Loose thyself from the bands of thy neck, O captive daughter of Zion” [2]. After having been bound by the neck to be dragged like one of the animals in captivity, these bands are loosed and the dignity of freedom returns to her, so that she lives as mistress of herself, with an inward authority. If sin humiliates man and drags him as it wishes, toying with him like a plaything in the hands of the evil enemy, then in Christ Jesus man lives as a king (Rev 1:6), holding authority over his heart, his thought, his feelings and his body.

52.1.2.en: In short, man rises from the death of sin, puts off his grave clothes and puts on the Lord Christ Himself as an everlasting garment; he refuses all uncleanness to bear within himself the righteousness of Christ; he shakes himself from the dust of the love of earthly things so that his soul may soar in the heavenly places; he rises from humiliation to sit at the right hand of God and enjoy fellowship in glory. His inner chains are loosed that he may enjoy the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

52.2.0.en: 3 For thus saith the LORD, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money. 4 For thus saith the Lord GOD, My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause. 5 Now therefore, what have I here, saith the LORD, that my people is taken away for nought? they that rule over them make them to howl, saith the LORD; and my name continually every day is blasphemed. 6 Therefore my people shall know my name: therefore they shall know in that day that I am he that doth speak: behold, it is I.

52.2.1.en: “For thus saith the LORD, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money” [3]. God did not sell His people to Babylon; rather, they sold themselves by forsaking God and disobeying Him, so He delivered them over to them. They received nothing in return, and God received nothing, because Babylon did not thank God who delivered this people to them as captives, but blasphemed Him. It is as though God did not wish to deliver them to Babylon, but they compelled Him by selling themselves to sin and to the abominations of idolatry.

52.2.2.en: God's people had earlier gone down to Egypt and sojourned there, and Pharaoh humiliated them; yet they did not learn, and sold themselves to Assyria, which oppressed them without cause, or without any provocation on the people's part against Assyria... Therefore God intervenes to save His people and to glorify His holy name.

52.2.3.en: We too delivered ourselves to the authority of sin and enslaved ourselves to the evil enemy for nothing... Now the Savior has come forward to free us without cost, not with gold or silver but with His precious Blood (Rev 5:9).

52.3.0.en: 7 How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth! 8 Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion. 9 Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem: for the LORD hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem. 10 The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

52.3.1.en: The good tidings of the people's return from captivity came from the Lord Himself, who reigned over His people [7], and voices of praise and singing rose up, not because of their return to their land but because of “the LORD's return to Zion” [8]. He came Himself to comfort His people, and made bare His holy arm to work to repair the ruin that had befallen His people and His city, to proclaim openly “in the eyes of all the nations” [10], that all the ends of the earth might glorify Him.

52.3.2.en: The speech here is chiefly about the joyful good tidings of the Gospel of salvation:

52.3.3.en: “How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth” [7]. What are these two beautiful feet but the Church of the New Testament, which speaks through the word of God (the mountains) to preach the Gospel and to proclaim that our Lord Jesus reigned from the wood and that He raised us up with Him?!

52.3.4.en: * He (Isaiah) sees how beautiful and fitting is the preaching of the Apostles who walk in (the Lord) who said “I am the way,” praising the feet of those who walk in the rational way of Jesus Christ, for through this door they enter to God (the Father). They bring good tidings, these whose feet are beautiful because Jesus has become for them (a way for their feet and the secret of their beauty).

52.3.5.en: Origen * When they preach to us the Gospel of this peace, of which he had prophesied: “How beautiful are the feet of them that publish peace, that bring good tidings of good” [7], each one of us begins to be a son of peace by his obedience and his faith in this Gospel, for he is justified by faith and receives peace with God.

52.3.6.en: * What are the feet of the Lord? They are the holy Evangelists!

52.3.7.en: * Through the beautiful feet of men who announce good things, the hearts of mankind have become an open way for the Lord.

52.4.0.en: 11 Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD. 12 For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward.

52.4.1.en: In the spirit of prophecy Isaiah saw the priests bearing the vessels of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken and which Belshazzar had used at the feast with contempt (Ezra 1:7-11), in a majestic procession that lasted about four months.

52.4.2.en: The prophet disclosed the secret of the majesty of this procession, namely:

52.4.3.en: a. On the negative side: departing from evil and continually going out from the captivity of sin: “Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD” [11]. It is a call to a continual going out, as the Apostle says: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, and will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters” (2 Cor 6:17-18).

52.4.4.en: * Paul counsels, saying: “Put away from among yourselves that wicked person,” “that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you” (1 Cor 5:13, 2). It is a terrible thing, truly terrible, the assembly of the wicked, for their plague spreads quickly and affects those who deal with them as though they were sick... “Evil communications corrupt good manners” (1 Cor 15:33)... May no one have a wicked friend.

52.5.0.en: St. John Chrysostom b. On the positive side: accepting God Himself as the leader of the procession; therefore we go out in calm and assurance, confident of the power of our Leader and of His protection of us all the way: “For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward” [12].

52.6.s.en: 5. The glory of the servant of the Lord:

52.6.0.en: 13 Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high. 14 As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men: 15 So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider.

52.6.1.en: Since He commanded that the Lord, the Savior, lead the procession, He presented to us a picture of the glory of the Savior, who became a servant in order to be glorified on our behalf and in our name; and the ancient Jews interpreted this text as referring to the Messiah.

52.6.2.en: a. “Behold, my servant”: the Word became flesh and was counted a servant of the Father as a representative of mankind, the Servant who obeys, so that in Him we are counted obedient to God.

52.6.3.en: b. “He shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high” [13]: He is the wisdom of God; for our sake He received the Spirit of wisdom and understanding resting upon Him (Isa 11:2), although the Holy Spirit is His own Spirit, inseparable from Him.

52.7.0.en: c. His appearance on the Cross astonished those in heaven and on earth: “As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men” [14]. This is what he will declare more clearly in the next chapter: “He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him...” (Isa 53:2-3).

52.7.1.en: d. Through this painful sight, as a sacrifice lifted up on the Cross, He sprinkled the Gentiles with His blood and so sanctified them to Himself, and shut the mouths of kings (perhaps meaning the powers of darkness), since they saw a salvation they had not understood before.
